title: TransBO: Hyperparameter Optimization via Two-Phase Transfer Learning

problem.claim: Hyperparameter optimization has become increasingly important because of the extensive use of machine learning models.

gap.claim: Existing HPO transfer approaches need to address complementary relationships among source tasks and dynamics during knowledge aggregation while accelerating current HPO tasks with past-task knowledge.

contributions.claim: TransBO is a two-phase transfer learning framework for hyperparameter optimization.
The framework jointly and adaptively extracts and aggregates source and target knowledge, with weights learned in a principled manner.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe TransBO as a novel framework designed to address complementary source-task relationships and dynamic knowledge aggregation in HPO.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments cover static and dynamic transfer learning settings as well as neural architecture search.
The authors report that TransBO outperforms state-of-the-art methods in the described experiments.

narrative_sequence.summary: The growing use of machine learning makes automatic hyperparameter optimization increasingly important.
Past HPO tasks can provide auxiliary knowledge for accelerating a current HPO task, following the tuning behavior of human experts.
The paper proposes TransBO, a two-phase transfer learning framework addressing complementary source tasks and dynamic knowledge aggregation.
TransBO jointly and adaptively extracts and aggregates source and target knowledge using principled learned weights.
Experiments across static and dynamic transfer settings and neural architecture search are reported to show superiority over state-of-the-art methods.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two phases or their algorithmic details.
Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are omitted.
The abstract does not identify the source-task similarity assumptions or transfer failure cases.
